With reference to [[display media]] and [[search media]], '''conversion tracking''' is the measurement of media performance with reference to campaign [[key performance indicators]] ([[key performance indicators|KPIs]]).

This process functions thanks to a [[JavaScript]] tracker or a [[Spy pixel|pixel tracker]]<ref>{{cite web|title=What is Pixel tracking definition ?|url=http://digitalmarketing-glossary.com/What-is-Pixel-tracking-definition|website=digitalmarketing-glossary.com|publisher=digitalmarketing-glossary|accessdate=20 September 2015|archive-date=25 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925134630/http://digitalmarketing-glossary.com/What-is-Pixel-tracking-definition|url-status=dead}}</ref> (when JavaScript is disabled, for instance in emails), which instantaneously records quantitative actions. Results are cross-referenced with the [[Key Performance Indicator|KPIs]], or measures of success, to gauge if the media inventory has achieved its targeting parameters. 

Common measures of success include: 
* [[Conversion rate]]: the ratio of orders to visitors<ref>{{cite web|title=Conversion Rate|url=https://www.marketingterms.com/dictionary/conversion_rate/|website=marketingterms|publisher=marketingterms.com|accessdate=20 September 2015}}</ref>
* Drop-off rate: the ratio of users that started processes but did not finish<ref>{{cite web|title=Difference Between Google Bounce Rate and Drop-offs |url=https://www.rankraiser.com/rankraiser/difference-between-google-bounce-rate-and-drop-offs/|website=rankraiser.com|date=28 February 2012 |publisher=rankraiser.com|accessdate=20 September 2015}}</ref>
* [[Click-through rate|Clickthrough rate]]: the ratio of total visitors with exposure to an advertisement, over those visitors who clicked through to the website<ref>{{cite web|title=click Through Rate|url=https://www.marketingterms.com/dictionary/clickthrough_rate/|website=marketingterms.com|publisher=marketingterms.com|accessdate=20 September 2015}}</ref>
* Registration rate: the ratio of website visitors who register to visitors leaving the site without registering again
* Interaction rate: the ratio of users,, who have been exposed to the ad to those who have interacted

The rise of programmatic buying has allowed faster and more efficient campaign optimization, therefore the examples above are a snapshot of the multitude of conversion metrics that a [[advertising campaign|campaign]] can achieve.

Measures of success ([[KPI-driven code analysis|KPIs]]) usually differ by the campaign and creative concept.<ref>{{cite web|title=Google ads Conversion Tracking Tag – A Complete Guide|url=https://www.theimpulsedigital.com/blog/google-ads-conversion-tracking-tag-a-complete-guide/|website=theimpulsedigital.com|date=4 June 2019 |publisher=impulsedigital|accessdate=20 June 2019}}</ref>
